 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Aday Mara is on the rise for the Oklahoma City Thunder this season, and the team hopes that he can continue his development throughout the campaign. Suddenly thrown into the fire, it does seem that the big man is filling the gap in OKC's defensive needs. He's also shining on offense, which is definitely something they need with multiple key stars out with injuries for the Thunder .
 From deterring opponents from scoring, blocking shots, crashing the glass, and even creating offensive opportunities, Mara has been a standout for Oklahoma City. He's providing a spark that you wouldn't expect from a rookie. Now he's proven that he can be a consistent player for the team, and that's the hope for him moving forward.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Mara Has Been a Beast for the Thunder
 Nov 7, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma City Thunder center Aday Mara (15) dunks against the Washington Wizards during the second half at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images
 Now averaging 8.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks per game this season, it's clear that Mara has excelled off OKC's bench . His numbers have gone up, and he has garnered a higher usage rate than ever. That says a lot for someone who's supposed to be getting fewer touches as a reserve before getting acclimated to bigger minutes.
 But with the Chet Holmgren injury , the Thunder's center spot finds itself with a vacant hole — something that Mara is now taking over in the star's absence. We are at a point where the Spanish center is showcasing his skill set well.
 At seven-foot-three, OKC getting Mara in the draft was a huge boon for the franchise on both sides. He's got the potential to be a high-impact defensive anchor alongside Holmgren, which is on-brand with the Thunder's identity. Let's not forget the fact that he's just 21 as well.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Rebounding Gets a Boost from Mara
 As a big man, you'd expect Mara to be a hulk on the glass, much like Victor Wembanyama . This month, the Thunder center has finished with more than five boards in his games. He's averaging 7.8 rebounds in this month alone.
 If that's not eye-catching enough for you, then it's worth noting that Mara's rebounding has been essential for the Thunder. In fact, thanks to his efforts, through 11 games, OKC is grabbing nearly five more defensive rebounds per game without Holmgren than with him (36.9 to 32.7). Of course, no Holmgren means Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein get more share at the center spot.
 That's a huge difference in cleaning up the glass, which is considered a weakness for OKC by some. With Mara, it does seem that the team can still stay competitive on that end. Now imagine if Holmgren comes back and pairs up with Mara moving forward.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Mara's Shot-Blocking is Elite for a Rookie
 To start off his career, Mara has logged 10 straight games with at least one block. He also leads all rookies in total blocks so far this season, which says a lot about his defensive prowess. Of course, some would say that it's less impressive given his height, but his level of hand-eye coordination at that height is hard to come by.
 With 20 blocks into the season ( tied for fifth-most ) as of the time of writing, it's not inconceivable that he could receive DPOY votes in his rookie season. Being a reliable defender for OKC, a team that prides itself on defense, is a huge boost to his case.
 At this point, he's probably knocking on the Rookie of the Year conversation, but that's still a long shot if we're going solely on his team having the best defense and having the most blocks among rookies.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Last Word
 Mara has so much to offer OKC this season. He's already shown that he can hit a triple on his first attempt (I-Hart has not made a single three in 28 attempts with the Thunder, mind you). Mara is expanding his game. He's shown flashes of playmaking, being able to go coast-to-coast when needed, and his superb shot-blocking ability makes him a huge asset for the team.
 But we're just 11 games into the season, and there's so much more for Mara to play, and for OKC to learn how to use him best.
